paragraphs: Alico was incorporated under the laws of the State of Florida in 1960. Alico is an agribusiness and land management company with a legacy of achievement and innovation in citrus and conservation. We focus on strategic land development opportunities and diversified agricultural operations. At September 30, 2025, we owned approximately 49,537 acres of land in eight Florida counties (Charlotte, Collier, DeSoto, Glades, Hardee, Hendry, Highlands and Polk), and approximately 44,700 acres of oil, gas and mineral rights throughout Florida. We hold these oil, gas and mineral rights on substantially all our owned acres, with additional mineral rights on other leased acres. Our principal lines of business are land management and citrus groves. See Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations, Recent Developments included in this Annual Report for a discussion of recent land sales activity.

We manage our land based upon its primary usage and review its performance based upon two primary classifications - Alico Citrus and Land Management and Other Operations. The Alico Citrus division includes activities related to planting, owning, cultivating and/or managing citrus groves to produce fruit for sale to fresh and processed citrus markets, including activities related to the purchase and resale of fruit and value-added services, which include contracting for the harvesting, marketing and hauling of citrus. However, the Alico Citrus division has substantially wound down operations after the 2024-2025 harvest due to environmental and financial challenges, as discussed further below. Land Management and Other Operations includes activities related to grazing and hunting leasing, management and/or conservation of unimproved native pastureland, activities related to rock mining royalties and other insignificant lines of business, and activities related to owning and/or leasing improved farmland. We present our financial results and the related discussion based upon our two business segments: (i) Alico Citrus and (ii) Land Management and Other Operations.

On January 6, 2025, we announced a Strategic Transformation (the "Strategic Transformation") in our business focus, to wind down our Alico Citrus division, to focus on a long-term diversified land usage and real estate development strategy. Due to increasing financial challenges from citrus greening disease and environmental factors for many seasons, we decided to not spend further material capital on our citrus operations and to wind down substantially all of our Citrus' primary operations after completion of the 2024-2025 harvest in April 2025. In connection with this Strategic Transformation, on January 3, 2025, our Board of Directors (the "Board") approved a reduction in our workforce by up to 172 employees, which occurred between January 6, 2025 and May 30, 2025. The Board's decision is part of cost-reduction initiatives aimed at providing investors with a greater return on capital that includes the benefits and stability of a conventional agriculture investment, with the optionality that comes with active land management.

In May 2025, we entered into a Mutual Contract Termination Agreement with Tropicana (the "Mutual Contract Termination Agreement"), terminating our agreement with them in its entirety following the fulfillment of all obligations under that agreement concerning the 2024/2025 Crop Year. All outstanding amounts were settled by June 30, 2025.

We regularly review our land-holdings to determine the best use of each parcel based upon our management expertise. Our total return profile is a combination of operating income potential and long-term appreciation. Land holdings that do not meet our total return criteria are considered surplus to our operations and efforts are being made ready to sell, develop, lease or exchange such land holdings for land considered to be more compatible with our business objectives and total return profile.
The operating activities on our land holdings and in which we engage as of September 30, 2025, are categorized in the following table:
Alico Citrus Citrus Groves 39,297 Citrus Cultivation Land Management and Other Operations Leasing and Conservation 9,583 Leasing and Conservation
Mining 657 Mining Lease and Office 10,240 Total 49,537 Alico Citrus

We own and manage citrus land in DeSoto, Polk, Collier, Hendry, Charlotte, Highlands, and Hardee Counties in the state of Florida and cultivate citrus trees to produce citrus for delivery to the fresh and processed citrus markets. Alico citrus groves total 39,297 gross acres or 79.3% of our land holdings, of which there are approximately 3,780 net tree acres dedicated to growing Citrus for the 2025-2026 harvest.

Sales to the processed market represented 96.0% and 92.0%, of Alico Citrus revenues for the years ended September 30, 2025 and 2024, respectively. The overall increase in the sales to the processed market as a percentage of citrus revenues is due to the termination of a grove management agreement, discussed below. Our sales to the fresh citrus market constituted 1.3% and 1.2% of our Alico Citrus revenues for the years ended September 30, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

The average pound solids per box was 4.82 and 4.83, for the years ended September 30, 2025 and 2024, respectively. We historically used multi-year contracts with citrus processors that may include pricing structures based on a floor and ceiling price. Therefore, if pricing in the market is favorable, relative to our floor price, we would benefit from the incremental difference between the floor and the final market price to the extent it does not exceed the ceiling price. However, the vast majority of our contracts for the 2024-2025 harvest season were fixed price contracts.

We supplied Tropicana, previously our largest customer, with citrus fruit under agreements entered into beginning in May 2020. The most recent agreements included: (1) an agreement effective August 31, 2023 through August 31, 2025 with fixed prices per pound solid and escalation provisions; and (2) a three‑year Orange Purchase Agreement effective June 5, 2024 through July 31, 2027, priced approximately 33%–50% above the prior year's average price for all citrus sold to Tropicana (together, the "Tropicana Agreements"). The Tropicana Agreements were terminated pursuant to the Mutual Contract Termination Agreement in May 2025, as described above.

On October 30, 2023, we entered into a grove management agreement (the "Grove Management Agreement") with unaffiliated third parties to provide citrus grove caretaking services for approximately 3,300 acres. Under the Grove Management Agreement, we were reimbursed for all costs and received a management fee based on acres covered. The Grove Management Agreement was terminated as of December 31, 2024 and as of September 30, 2025, we had no significant third-party grove management agreements. Revenues from our grove management services represented 2.2% and 6.3% of our total citrus revenues for the years ended September 30, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

During the year ended September 30, 2025, we sold approximately 2,796 acres of citrus and ranch land for approximately $23,807 and recognized a gain of $20,319. During the year ended September 30, 2024, we sold approximately 18,354 acres of ranch and citrus land for $86,217 and recognized a gain of $81,416.

paragraphs: Our business and results of operations are subject to numerous risks and uncertainties, many of which are beyond our control. The following is a description of key known factors that we believe may materially affect our business, financial condition, results of operations or cash flows. They should be considered carefully, together with the information set forth elsewhere in this Annual Report, and with our other filings with the SEC. The realization of any of these risks and uncertainties could have a material adverse effect on our reputation, business, financial condition, results of operations, growth and future prospects, as well as our ability to accomplish our strategic objectives.

If we are unable to successfully develop and execute our strategic growth initiatives, or if they do not adequately address the challenges or opportunities we face, our business, financial condition and prospects may be adversely affected.

Our success is dependent, in part, on our ability to identify, develop and execute appropriate strategic growth initiatives that will enable us to achieve sustainable growth in the long term. The implementation of our strategic initiatives is subject to both the risks affecting our business generally and the inherent risks associated with implementing new strategies. These strategic initiatives have included, for example, beginning in 2023 a multi-year entitlement process for our approximately 4,600-acre grove near Fort Myers, in Collier County, which has included, but is not limited to, the completion of environmental assessments, the development of conservation strategies, the preparation of market assessments to facilitate planning and beginning to conduct selective stakeholder outreach efforts. In addition, on January 6, 2025, we announced a Strategic Transformation in the Company's business focus, to wind down our Alico Citrus division, which holds our citrus production operations, to focus on our long-term diversified land usage and real estate development strategy (the "Strategic Transformation"). Due to increasing financial challenges from citrus greening disease and environmental factors for many seasons, we have decided to not spend further material capital on our citrus operations and plan to substantially wind down Alico Citrus' primary operations after completion of the 2024-2025 harvest in April 2025, including reducing most of our citrus production workforce. Moreover, in May 2025, we entered into a Mutual Contract Termination Agreement with Tropicana, terminating our agreement with Tropicana in its entirety following the fulfillment of all obligations under that agreement concerning the 2024/2025 Crop Year and all outstanding amounts had been settled by June 30, 2025. We expect to maintain our commitment to the Florida agriculture industry through diversified farming operations on nearly all our land holdings following this citrus production transition. We also expect to entitle certain parcels of our land for commercial and residential development.
Successfully executing our diversified land usage and real estate development strategy will depend on many factors, including our ability to:
•secure necessary regulatory approvals and permits for land development projects; •effectively manage and allocate resources to new business initiatives;
•attract and retain skilled personnel with expertise in diversified land usage and real estate development;

paragraphs: Alico 於佛羅裏達州根據該州法律於 1960 年成立。Alico 是一家農業與土地管理公司，擁有在柑橘與保育方面成就與創新之遺產。我們專注於戰略性土地開發機會與多元化農業業務。於 2025 年 9 月 30 日，我們擁有約 49,537 英畝土地，位於佛羅裏達州八個縣（查爾斯頓、科利爾、迪塞託、格萊德斯、哈迪、亨德里、高地斯與波克），以及約 44,700 英畝的石油、天然氣與礦物權。我們在 substantially all 我們所擁有土地上持有這些石油、天然氣與礦物權，並在其他租賃土地上持有額外的礦物權。我們的主要業務為土地管理與柑橘園。請參閱本年度報告第 7 項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」，以及包含在本年度報告中的「近期發展」，以瞭解近期土地銷售活動之討論。

我們根據土地的主要用途來管理土地，並根據兩種主要分類來評估其表現 - Alico 柑橘與土地管理，以及其他業務。Alico 柑橘部門包括與種植、擁有、栽培與/或管理柑橘園以生產水果，供應給鮮果與加工柑橘市場相關之活動，包括與購買與轉售水果及增值服務相關之活動，這些服務包括與採收、行銷與運輸柑橘之契約。然而，由於環境與財務挑戰，Alico 柑橘部門在 2024-2025 收割季結束後已大幅縮減業務，如進一步討論。土地管理與其他業務包括與放牧與狩獵租賃、未改善原生牧場地之管理與/或保育、與岩石採礦 royalties 及其他無足輕重之業務相關之活動，以及與擁有與/或租賃改善農地相關之活動。我們根據我們的兩大業務分部來呈現財務結果與相關討論：(i) Alico 柑橘，以及 (ii) 土地管理與其他業務。

於 2025 年 1 月 6 日，我們宣佈了一項業務重點轉型（"業務重點轉型"），以逐步結束 Alico 柑橘部門，專注於長期多元化土地使用與房地產開發策略。由於柑橘黃龍病與環境因素導致財務挑戰持續增加，我們決定不再投入進一步重大資金於柑橘業務，並在 2024-2025 收割季結束（2025 年 4 月）後，大幅結束柑橘業務的主體運作。根據此業務重點轉型，於 2025 年 1 月 3 日，我們董事會（"董事會"）批准減少最多 172 名員工，此員工減少於 2025 年 1 月 6 日至 2025 年 5 月 30 日之間進行。董事會的決定是成本削減計畫的一部分，旨在為投資人提供更高的資本回報，包括傳統農業投資的效益與穩定性，以及活躍土地管理所帶來的選擇性。
於 2025 年 5 月，我們與 Tropicana 簽訂了「雙方契約終止協議」（"雙方契約終止協議"），終止我們與他們之間的全部協議，此協議在 2024/2025 穀物年度所有義務履行後終止。所有未結清金額於 2025 年 6 月 30 日前結清。
我們定期審查我們的土地持有狀況，以根據我們的管理專業判斷每塊土地的最佳用途。我們的總回報架構是營運收入潛力與長期增值的結合。不符合我們總回報標準的土地持有被視為與我們的業務運作無關，並正在進行準備以出售、開發、租賃或交換這些土地持有，以換取更符合我們業務目標與總回報架構的土地。
截至 2025 年 9 月 30 日，我們在土地持有上進行的營運活動如下表所示：
Alico 柑橘 柑橘園 39,297 柑橘種植 土地管理與其他業務 租賃與保育 9,583 租賃與保育
採礦 657 採礦租賃與辦公室 10,240 總計 49,537 Alico 柑橘
本公司擁有並管理位於佛羅裏達州德索托、波克、科利爾、亨德里、查爾羅特、高地斯與哈迪縣的柑橘土地，並種植柑橘樹以生產柑橘，供應至鮮食與加工柑橘市場。Alico 柑橘園總計 39,297 畝（毛地），佔本公司土地持有量的 79.3%，其中約 3,780 畝為種植柑橘以供應 2025-2026 收割季使用。

2025 年 9 月 30 日財務年度，銷售至加工市場的收入佔 Alico 柑橘營收的 96.0%，2024 年 9 月 30 日財務年度則為 92.0%。銷售至加工市場佔柑橘營收比例的整體增加，係因終止了一項園區管理協議，詳情如下所述。本公司銷售至鮮食柑橘市場的收入，分別佔 Alico 柑橘營收的 1.3% 與 1.2%，為 2025 年 9 月 30 日與 2024 年 9 月 30 日財務年度的資料。
2025 年 9 月 30 日財務年度，每箱平均固體重量為 4.82 磅，2024 年 9 月 30 日財務年度為 4.83 磅。本公司歷來與柑橘加工廠簽訂多年合約，這些合約可能包含基於地板價格與天花板價格的定價結構。因此，若市場價格優於我們的地板價格，我們將受益於地板價格與最終市場價格之間的差額，但以不超過天花板價格為限。然而，2024-2025 收割季的絕大多數合約為固定價格合約。

本公司自 2020 年 5 月起與 Tropicana（本公司過去最大客戶）簽訂協議，供應柑橘水果。最近的協議包括：(1) 一項自 2023 年 8 月 31 日至 2025 年 8 月 31 日的協議，包含固定每磅固體價格與調漲條款；以及 (2) 一項自 2024 年 6 月 5 日至 2027 年 7 月 31 日的三年橙子採購協議，價格約為前一年平均價格的 33%–50% 高（合稱為「Tropicana 協議」）。Tropicana 協議於 2025 年 5 月根據雙方合約終止協議終止，詳情如上所述。

2023 年 10 月 30 日，本公司與無關第三方簽訂園區管理協議（「園區管理協議」），以提供約 3,300 畝的柑橘園區照護服務。根據園區管理協議，本公司將所有成本予以報銷，並根據覆蓋畝數收取管理費。園區管理協議於 2024 年 12 月 31 日終止，截至 2025 年 9 月 30 日，本公司無重大第三方園區管理協議。本公司園區管理服務收入，分別佔 2025 年 9 月 30 日與 2024 年 9 月 30 日財務年度總柑橘收入的 2.2% 與 6.3%。
2025 年 9 月 30 日財務年度，本公司出售約 2,796 畝的柑橘與農場土地，價值約 23,807 美元，並確認獲利 20,319 美元。2024 年 9 月 30 日財務年度，本公司出售約 18,354 畝的農場與柑橘土地，價值 86,217 美元，並確認獲利 81,416 美元。

headings: 與我們業務相關的風險
我們的員工減編可能無法達到預期的成效，並可能導致未預期的後果及額外成本。
土地開發業務競爭激烈，我們無法保證我們將維持目前的市場佔有率。
我們的聲譽受損可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
我們使用淨營業虧損結轉及某些其他稅務屬性的能力可能受到限制。
我們在農業業務方面面臨顯著的競爭。
我們的獲利對土地銷售、租賃及開發活動的供給、需求及價格動態，以及任何剩餘農產品，均相當敏感。
氣候變遷，或用以應對氣候變遷的法律、法規或市場措施，可能對我們的業務及營運產生負面影響。
ESG 事項，包括與我們員工及永續性相關的議題，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運成果及現金流產生不利影響，並損害我們的聲譽。
遵守適用的環境法規可能會顯著提高我們的營運成本，這可能會降低我們的利潤。
若我們失去關鍵員工，可能會對我們的業務產生不利影響。
通貨膨脹可能對我們的營運產生顯著不利影響。
我們因成為上市公司而產生更高的成本。
我們的業務受到關於隱私權及資料保護的複雜且不斷演進的法律與法規的影響。
我們的農產品受到供需價格的影響，而此價格並不可預測。
我們面臨產品汙染及產品責任索償的風險。
本公司之農業營運受水資源使用規範之限制，可能影響本公司對水資源之取得。
使用肥料、農藥、除草劑及其他潛在危險物質之責任，可能增加本公司之成本。
農產品或原物料成本之增加，例如燃料及化學品成本，可能對本公司之營運成果造成不利影響。
本公司受運輸風險之影響。
與本公司負債相關之風險
paragraphs: 本公司之業務及營運成果受許多風險與不確定因素影響，許多因素為本公司所無法控制。以下為關鍵已知因素之描述，本公司認為這些因素可能對本公司之業務、財務狀況、營運成果或現金流產生重大影響。應與本年度年報其他資訊及本公司向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）所提交之其他申報文件一併謹慎考量。任何這些風險與不確定因素實現，可能對本公司之聲譽、業務、財務狀況、營運成果、成長與未來展望，以及本公司達成戰略目標之能力產生重大不利影響。
若本公司無法成功開發並執行戰略成長計畫，或這些計畫未能充分應對我們所面臨之挑戰或機會，則本公司之業務、財務狀況與前景可能受到不利影響。

本公司之成功在部分程度上取決於本公司識別、開發並執行適當之戰略成長計畫之能力，以實現長期可持續之成長。本公司戰略計畫之執行受一般業務風險影響，以及執行新策略所固有之風險。這些戰略計畫包括，例如，自2023年起，針對位於佛羅裏達州科利爾縣福特米爾斯附近約4,600英畝之園區，進行多年度之權利取得程序，此程序包括但不僅限於環境評估之完成、保育策略之制定、市場評估之準備以協助規劃，以及開始進行選擇性利害關係人之接觸工作。此外，本公司於2025年1月6日宣佈進行戰略轉型，將本公司業務重點轉向長期多元化土地使用與不動產開發策略（"戰略轉型"）。由於柑橘黃龍病及環境因素在多個季節造成財務挑戰，本公司已決定不再投入重大資本於柑橘業務，並計畫在2024-2025年收穫期結束後，即2025年4月，大幅縮減Alico Citrus之主要業務運作，包括減少大多數柑橘生產員工。此外，本公司於2025年5月與Tropicana簽訂相互契約終止協議，終止與Tropicana之全部協議，此協議在2024/2025年作物年度所有義務履行完畢，且所有未結清金額於2025年6月30日前已結清。本公司預期在柑橘生產轉型後，透過多元化農業業務在幾乎所有土地持有上維持對佛羅裏達州農業產業之承諾。本公司亦預期對部分土地取得商業與住宅開發之權利。
成功執行多元化土地使用與不動產開發策略，將取決於許多因素，包括本公司之能力：
•取得土地開發專案所需之必要法規核准與許可；•有效地管理與分配資源至新業務計畫；
•吸引並留住具多元化土地使用與不動產開發專業知識之專業人才；
